keyframe_review.note: 716,066 km2: Sweden, Finland and northern Estonia. The page's only area is a body-text sentence, 'The land area of Sweden was 1,100,000 km2.', with no year (read here as the realm after the Treaty of Cardis, 1661); against that the ratio is 0.65, fine for a realm that later grew. The page: 'The beginning of the period is usually taken as the reign of Gustavus Adolphus, who ascended the throne in 1611.' Shape unchanged but it holds 1612-1616 only: from March 1617 the 1619 shape applies. The 26 cells counted as Norway lie along the northern and western frontier; no opened page explains them. Estonia is not dated on the pages opened (the Stolbovo page has Russia renounce all claims to Estonia and Livonia in 1617).

correction.text: Shape unchanged; holds 1612-1616 only (Ingria and Kexholm are Swedish from March 1617)

keyframe_review.note: Shape right, years wrong: 'Sweden gained the province of Kexholm in Karelia and the province of Ingria – including the fortress of Nöteborg' at the Treaty of Stolbovo, 'The meeting took place on 9 March [O.S. 27 February] 1617', two years before Cliopatria's shape begins. The shape adds 118 cells on the Russian side of the modern border against the 1612 shape. Cliopatria's 1612 shape holds 2 cells of a 25 km circle round Göteborg and the 1619 shape 4: the shape fits a Danish-held Älvsborg to 1618 (ledger 1613-1619).

correction.text: Shape unchanged; holds 1617-1628 (Ingria with Nöteborg and Kexholm from 9 March 1617)
The 1619 shape plus Livonia north of the Daugava with Riga, from the Truce of Mitawa (November 1622)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'Riga capitulated on 25 September' 1621 and the Truce of Mitawa of November 1622 cedes 'Livonia north of the Daugava' (infobox: 'Commonwealth cedes Livonia north of the Daugava river'); Cliopatria's 1629 shape is the 1619 shape plus 236 Livonian cells, so it is used for 1622-1628. Pomerania (1630) and the Prussian ports (Altmark 1629) are not yet Swedish.

Livonia north of the Daugava is Swedish from the Truce of Mitawa in November 1622 ('Under the terms of the Truce of Mitawa in November 1622, they ceded Livonia north of the Daugava') and the Altmark truce ('signed on 26 September [O.S. 16 September] 1629'; 'The truce allowed Sweden to retain control of Livonia') confirms it, so Cliopatria's shape starts seven years late (new keyframe swedish-empire_1622). Added to the base shape: the Prussian coastal cities ('kept the coastal cities'; the page names only Elbing) and Pomerania, which the Swedes occupied from 1630.

correction.text: The 1629 shape plus Pomerania (from 1630) and the Prussian coastal cities Sweden kept after Altmark; holds 1629-1631

keyframe_review.note: 917 extra cells (lon 7.3-19.1, lat 47.4-54.1, Germany and western Poland) are land held by Swedish armies after 'victories at Breitenfeld in September 1631, then Rain in April 1632'. Sweden annexed none of it: at the Peace of Westphalia 'Sweden gains Wismar, Wolin, Western Pomerania, and Bremen-Verden'. The zone is occupation (ledger, April 1632 to 1635), not territory, so the base shape is the 1636 shape plus the Prussian ports Sweden kept until 1635 (Truce of Altmark page: 'Sweden gave up the Prussian ports' in 1635).

correction.text: Sweden, Finland, Livonia, Estonia, Ingria, Kexholm and Pomerania without the German zone held by the armies; plus the Prussian coastal cities until 1635; holds 1632-1635

keyframe_review.note: The 29 German cells (lon 12.6-14.7, lat 53.2-54.7) are Western Pomerania, occupied by Sweden from 1630, Swedish rule from the end of the ducal house on 10 March 1637 (ledger) and confirmed at Westphalia. The Prussian ports are gone ('Sweden gave up the Prussian ports', 1635, Altmark page). The Peace of Prague is 1635 on the Thirty Years' War page, and Cliopatria's 1636 start follows it.

+120 cells over 1636 (lon 12.6-15.2, lat 50.4-54.2): Banér's campaigns ('In April 1639, Banér defeated the Saxons at Chemnitz, then invaded Bohemia in May'). The land is occupied, not annexed; the base shape is the 1636 shape.

correction.text: The 1636 shape (Sweden, Finland, Livonia, Estonia, Ingria, Kexholm, Western Pomerania); the German zone is occupation; holds 1640-1641

keyframe_review.note: +163 cells over 1640 (lon 10.8-15.2, lat 50.7-54.3) round Leipzig: 'The Swedes captured Leipzig in December, although they failed to take Freiberg' (the fetch summary dated it 1642). Occupation, not territory.

correction.text: The 1636 shape; the German zone is occupation; holds 1642-1644

keyframe_review.note: 13 August 1645: Denmark-Norway ceded Jämtland, Härjedalen, Gotland and Saaremaa (Ösel), Sweden received Halland for 30 years and Verden and Bremen 'were transferred from Danish to Swedish control'. Those gains are the +363 Swedish cells and Ösel in the shape. The 262 further German cells (lon 10.8-15.2, lat 50.7-54.3) are army-held land that Cliopatria drops in 1648; they are occupation. Base shape: the part of the 1645 shape that survives into 1648.

correction.text: The 1645 shape without the German army zone: the 1636 shape plus Gotland, Ösel, Jämtland, Härjedalen, Halland and Bremen-Verden; holds 1645-1647

keyframe_review.note: Western Pomerania (Swedish rule since 1637, ledger), Wismar and Bremen-Verden as Sweden's German gains confirmed on 24 October 1648 ('Sweden received an indemnity of five million thalers, the imperial territories of Swedish Pomerania'; infobox 'Sweden gains Wismar, Wolin, Western Pomerania, and Bremen-Verden'). Cliopatria starts the shape in 1648, the year of the treaties.

+6 cells on the Gold Coast (lon -1.2..0.0, lat 5.2..5.8). The page says only 'A string of Swedish forts and trading posts was constructed along the coast of West Africa', with no date; Cliopatria draws the Gold Coast in 1653-1658 and 1662-1669 but not in 1659-1661. The colony belongs to the swedish-gold-coast dossier, so the base shape here omits it. New Sweden ('founded in the valley of the Delaware River in 1638') is not drawn by Cliopatria at all.

correction.text: The 1653 shape without the Gold Coast forts, which the colony dossier carries; holds 1653-1655 (the Russian occupation of the Baltic edge takes land out from 1656)
The 1653 shape without the Gold Coast forts and without the Baltic edge held by Russia; holds 1656-1657

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. From July 1656 Russia holds Swedish ground in Ingria, Livonia and Finland (ledger occupation 1656-1661); Cliopatria drops the land only in its 1659 shape, so the base shape for 1656-1657 is the 1653 shape without the Gold Coast and without that edge. The Roskilde cessions are still to come.

correction.text: The 1659 shape used for 1658 (Roskilde gains, Baltic edge still occupied by Russia)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Treaty of Roskilde, 'signed on 8 March 1658': Scania, Blekinge, Halland, Bohuslän, Trøndelag and Bornholm are Swedish from March 1658, a year before Cliopatria's 1659 shape begins; the Baltic edge is still in Russian hands (Valiesar, 20 December 1658).

Treaty of Roskilde, 'signed on 8 March 1658': Scania, Blekinge, Halland, Bohuslän, Trøndelag 'then including Nordmøre and Romsdal' and Bornholm go to Sweden. The 284 extra Norwegian cells are Sør-Trøndelag (101), Nord-Trøndelag (122) and Møre og Romsdal (46); three cells are Bornholm. Shape unchanged and holds 1659; Cliopatria starts it a year after Roskilde (new keyframe swedish-empire_1658). The Baltic edge is smaller than in 1662 (about 35 cells in Finland, 30 in Estonia, 65 on the Russian side), land Russia occupied from July 1656 and 'surrendered' at Cardis in 1661 (ledger occupation 1656-1661, Russo-Swedish War page).

correction.text: Shape unchanged; holds 1659 (Roskilde gains, Baltic edge still reduced); 1658 and 1660-1661 have keyframes of their own

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'The Treaty of Copenhagen restored Bornholm to Denmark and Trøndelag to Norway in 1660' while 'the other provinces transferred in Roskilde remained Swedish' (27 May 1660 on the Swedish Empire page). Cliopatria keeps both in the shape to 1661. The 1659 shape runs to 1661 in Cliopatria, so this keyframe holds 1660-1661; the Baltic edge returns at Cardis on 2 July 1661.

correction.text: The 1659 shape without Trøndelag with Nordmøre and Romsdal, and without Bornholm; holds 1660-1661

keyframe_review.note: 921,329 km2 against the page's body-text 1,100,000 km2 (no year; the realm after Cardis): ratio 0.84, fine. 2 July 1661, Treaty of Cardis: 'the Tsar surrendered the Baltic provinces to Sweden'; the +143 cells over 1659 are the land Russia had occupied since 1656, returned (ledger occupation_end), not a gain. The 6 Gold Coast cells are removed as in 1653.

correction.text: The 1662 shape without the Gold Coast forts; holds 1661-1669

keyframe_review.note: 920,783 km2, no change of land. The Scanian War (1675-1679) took Swedish Pomerania and Bremen away without any change in Cliopatria's shape; the ledger carries it as occupation.

919,088 km2; the 1679 settlements 'Sweden received almost full restitution of its German territory'. The two-cell difference from 1670 in Germany and Poland is the strip east of the Oder that Brandenburg kept in 1679 (ledger loss 1679-6).

Shape unchanged but it holds 1702 only: 'Russian victories at Erastfer and Nöteborg (Shlisselburg) provided access to Ingria in 1703' and Peter 'captured the Swedish fortress of Nyen, guarding the mouth of the River Neva'.

correction.text: Shape unchanged; holds 1702 only

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Ingria goes to Russia in 1703; Cliopatria's 1706 shape also drops 66 cells further south (lon 23.9-30.6, lat 56.4-60.6, eastern Livonia and Estonia), of which Narva (14 cells) falls on 20 August 1704 and the rest is undated on the pages opened, so they are placed with the dated Ingria loss. The 28 cells Cliopatria adds in 1706 (Saxony) are occupation and stay out of the base shape.

correction.text: Sweden, Finland, Estonia and Livonia without Ingria and the eastern edge, but with Narva (lost 20 August 1704); holds 1703
Sweden, Finland, Estonia and Livonia without Ingria, Narva, Tartu and the eastern edge, and without the Saxon strip; holds 1704-1705

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Tartu fell on 24 June 1704 ('captured Tartu on 24 June') and Narva on 20 August 1704; Cliopatria's 1706 shape still holds Tartu (its circle lies outside the 66 dropped cells) and keeps it to 1713, so Tartu is taken out of the base shape here and in the 1706 and 1709 keyframes.

'he finally had to invade Augustus' hereditary Saxony', 'forcing him to acknowledge defeat in the Treaty of Altranstädt (October 1706)'; 'Charles XII moved from Saxony into Russia to confront Peter' in 1707. The 28 Saxon cells are occupation for 1706-1707 only and Cliopatria keeps them to 1708; the base shape is the 1703 shape.

correction.text: The 1703 shape without Tartu: no Saxon strip; holds 1706-1708 (the Saxon occupation is a ledger event, 1706-1707)

keyframe_review.note: 65 cells in Ukraine (lon 25.5-33.7, lat 49.8-57.5) are drawn as Swedish. The page records Mazepa's defection in October 1708 'with several thousand followers' and Poltava in 1709 after which Charles fled to the Ottoman Empire; it records no Swedish-ruled land in Ukraine. The Baltic lands are still drawn in full, correct for 1709 (lost in 1710). Tartu fell on 24 June 1704 (ledger), so it is out of the base shape.

correction.text: The 1709 shape without the Ukrainian strip and without Tartu; holds 1709 only

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. In 1710 'the Russian forces captured Riga', 'Russia captured Viborg' and Tallinn fell 'in the autumn of 1710', but Cliopatria keeps the Baltic provinces to 1712. Base shape: the 1713 shape (no Baltic provinces) plus the German possessions, which Cliopatria still draws and which stayed Swedish until the cessions of 1719-1720.

correction.text: Sweden and Finland without Estonia, Livonia and Vyborg, plus Swedish Germany (Pomerania, Wismar, Bremen-Verden)
Sweden and Finland without the Baltic provinces and without Danish-occupied Bremen-Verden, with southern Swedish Pomerania; holds 1712

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'In 1712 ... Denmark-Norway occupied plague stricken Bremen-Verden' (ledger occupation, hatched), so Bremen-Verden leaves the base shape while southern Pomerania stays Swedish (Prussia occupies it only in 1715). Base: Cliopatria's 1713 shape plus southern Swedish Pomerania.

Cliopatria's 1713 shape drops Bremen-Verden and southern Pomerania, which the pages date differently: Denmark-Norway occupied Bremen-Verden in 1712 (ledger), Prussia took the south of Swedish Pomerania only in 1715, and Sweden ceded them in 1719 and January 1720. The shape is used for 1713 with southern Pomerania added back. Finland is still drawn Swedish, but 'By 1714, Russia had occupied Finland'. The table lists the shape to 1717; the keyframes from 1714 replace it. correction.text: The 1713 shape plus southern Swedish Pomerania; holds 1713 only (Bremen-Verden is Danish-occupied; Finland follows in the 1714 keyframe)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'The brutal occupation period of Finland in 1714-1721 is known as the Great Wrath'; the occupied Finland is drawn hatched (ledger occupation 1714 to 1721), so the base shape is Cliopatria's 1718 shape, which already lacks it.

correction.text: Sweden without occupied Finland (northern fringe only), the 1718 shape, plus southern Swedish Pomerania; holds 1714
The 1718 shape: Sweden without Finland, with northern Swedish Pomerania and Wismar; holds 1715

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Prussia declares war in summer 1715 and occupies southern Swedish Pomerania (ledger); Stralsund and Rügen fall only in November-December 1715, so the 1718 shape (which holds the north and Wismar) fits 1715.

correction.text: The 1718 shape without northern Swedish Pomerania and Wismar (Danish-occupied); holds 1716-1717

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Stralsund and Rügen fell in November-December 1715 and Wismar in 1716 ('Swedish Wismar surrendered to the allies'); the 1713 and 1718 shapes keep them (15 German cells) although the land was occupied until 1721. They are taken out of the base shape and drawn by the occupation events.

2,691 cells against 4,184 in 1713: Finland (1,494 cells) is out because of the Russian occupation, correct for 1718-1720 ('Finland was returned to Sweden' in 1721). Cliopatria starts this absence in 1718, four years after the page's 1714. The 15 German cells (Stralsund, Rügen, Wismar) are Danish-occupied in 1718-1720 (ledger) and come out of the base shape; they return with the 1721 shape.

correction.text: The 1718 shape without northern Swedish Pomerania and Wismar (Danish-occupied until January 1721); holds 1718-1720

keyframe_review.note: Finland returns at the Treaty of Nystad ('30 August 1721 (OS)'); Sweden loses 'Estonia, Livonia, Ingria, Kexholm and a portion of Karelia'. 800,952 km2, the same outline as 1713; the Baltic provinces had been lost de facto in 1710. Sweden keeps 'Wismar and northern Swedish Pomerania' (15 German cells).

18 August 1743, Treaty of Åbo: Sweden 'ceded to Russia the areas east of the Kymi River with the fortress of Olofsborg' and 'the towns of Villmanstrand (Lappeenranta) and Fredrikshamn (Hamina)'. The shape has 51 fewer Finnish cells than 1721, about 13,000 km2; Cliopatria starts it a year after the treaty.

The one-year 1762 shape adds about 12 German cells (lat 53.46) and 3,000 km2. The Pomeranian War page: 'The war was formally ended on 22 May 1762 by the Peace of Hamburg ... Prussia and Sweden were restored to the status quo ante bellum', infobox 'Status quo ante bellum', and the Swedes 'withdrew into Swedish Pomerania' in late 1759; no Swedish-held ground in 1762 is on the page, so the 1763 shape is used. The war is a contest event, 1757-1762.

correction.text: The 1763 shape (status quo ante); the 12 extra German cells of the 1762 shape are not supported

keyframe_review.note: The outline returns to the 1744 shape (790,048 km2) and holds to 1806. The Russo-Swedish War of 1788-1790 ended 'by the Treaty of Värälä on 14 August 1790' with 'Status quo ante bellum: All conquests made by both sides are returned', so no land changes; the Pomeranian War (1757-1762) likewise ended in the status quo ante. Verified for these two wars only.

correction.text: The 1763 shape without Swedish Pomerania (French-occupied); holds 1807

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. French troops occupy Swedish Pomerania 'beginning in 1807' (ledger occupation to 1810); Finland is still Swedish in 1807 (the Russian invasion is February 1808), so the base is the 1763 shape without Pomerania.

correction.text: Sweden without Finland (Russian-occupied) and without Swedish Pomerania (French-occupied); holds 1808

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Russia crosses the border on 21 February 1808 and 'By November 1808, Russian forces had overrun all of Finland' (ledger occupation); Pomerania is French-occupied. Base: the 1809 shape without Germany.

'Finland was ceded to Russia in 1809' (Swedish Empire page); the Treaty of Fredrikshamn is dated 17 September 1809 on the Finnish War page ('Sweden loses Finland, Åland, a part of Lapland and a part of West Bothnia'). 463,710 km2 against 790,048 km2: Sweden proper with the five Finnish cells of the Torne valley and Swedish Pomerania, which is drawn separately for 1809 because France occupied it until 1810.

correction.text: The 1809 shape without Swedish Pomerania (French-occupied until the Treaty of Paris of 1810); holds 1809
Shape unchanged; holds 1810-1813 (Swedish Pomerania returned by France)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'Under the Treaty of Paris, signed in 1810, the territory was returned to Sweden': Swedish Pomerania is Swedish again, so Cliopatria's 1809 shape holds for 1810-1813.

The Treaty of Kiel (14 January 1814) gave 'Swedish Pomerania' to Denmark in return for Norway, but Sweden 'refused to hand over Swedish Pomerania': Charles XIII released the Pomeranian subjects on 1 October 1815 and the province was handed over on 23 October 1815. Cliopatria drops Pomerania in 1814; it stays Swedish for this year. The 13 Caribbean cells (lon -61.8, lat 15.9, Guadeloupe) are removed: 'On 3 March 1813, Guadeloupe was ceded by Britain to Sweden', but the page does not say Sweden ever took possession, the island 'was returned to France' by the Treaty of Paris of 1814, and Sweden received 24 million francs on 13 August 1814 instead. No Swedish Guadeloupe dossier is wanted unless a page shows Swedish rule. Norway is not Swedish land in 1814 (union 4 November 1814).

correction.text: The 1814 shape without Guadeloupe, plus Swedish Pomerania, which Sweden kept until 23 October 1815

ledger.note: 1612: the Swedish Empire begins with the reign of Gustavus Adolphus. 'The beginning of the period is usually taken as the reign of Gustavus Adolphus, who ascended the throne in 1611'; Cliopatria opens the row in 1612. Same crown and state as the Kingdom of Sweden (see notes).

Denmark–Norway declared war upon Sweden and invaded', and its troops 'laid siege to the city of Kalmar, ultimately taking it'; in early 1612 they 'eventually conquered two fortresses', Älvsborg and Gullberg. Mirrors denmark-norway L8; Cliopatria draws none of it.

region.text: Novgorod

ledger.note: Began in July 1611, before this dossier's first year: 'In July 1611, a Swedish expeditionary corps under Jacob De la Gardie captured Novgorod.' Swedish-held until Stolbovo (1617). Mirrors tsardom-of-russia L42; Cliopatria does not draw it.

region.text: Kalmar and the fortresses of Älvsborg and Gullberg

region.text: Älvsborg and Gullberg, Sweden's only outlet on the North Sea

Cliopatria's 1612 shape holds 2 cells of the Göteborg circle and its 1619 shape 4, which fits a Danish-held Älvsborg to 1618. Mirrors denmark-norway L10.

'Sweden gained the province of Kexholm in Karelia and the province of Ingria – including the fortress of Nöteborg'; 'The meeting took place on 9 March [O.S. 27 February] 1617'; Novgorod and other gains were returned and Russia renounced Estonia and Livonia. Cliopatria shows it from 1619.

region.text: Gdov

ledger.note: 9 March 1617: Gdov is returned at Stolbovo ('restored Novgorod and Gdov'). Mirrors tsardom-of-russia L47.

region.text: Älvsborg and Gullberg

region.text: Livonia north of the Daugava with Riga

ledger.note: August 1621: 'a Swedish army landed near Pärnu' (19 August 1621); 'Riga capitulated on 25 September' after a siege from 29 August. Mirrors swedish-livonia L0/L1; Cliopatria draws Livonia Swedish only from 1629.

region.text: Livonia north of the Daugava with Riga

ledger.note: November 1622: 'Under the terms of the Truce of Mitawa in November 1622, they ceded Livonia north of the Daugava'; the truce was prolonged to March 1625 and the fighting resumed in 1625.

region.text: Livonia north of the Daugava, including Riga

ledger.note: November 1622: the Truce of Mitawa cedes Livonia north of the Daugava (infobox 'Commonwealth cedes Livonia north of the Daugava river'). The Altmark page of 26 September 1629 ('The truce allowed Sweden to retain control of Livonia') confirms it, so the single gain of Livonia is dated here and the former 1629 gain is removed; Cliopatria's shape starts in 1629.

1629: Sweden keeps the Prussian coast. 'Sweden also evacuated most of the Duchy of Prussia but kept the coastal cities'; the page names no city but Elbing (as a port with Swedish shipping tolls), so the region is a radius round Elbing.

region.text: the coastal cities of the Duchy of Prussia
the Duchy of Pomerania, occupied by Swedish troops

ledger.note: 1630: Sweden occupies the duchy: infobox 'Occupied by Gustavus Adolphus of Sweden: 1630'; the Thirty Years' War page has him land 'in Pomerania in June 1630 with nearly 18,000 troops' and the Swedish Empire page has Pomerania 'in its possession since the Treaty of Stettin (1630)'. Replaces the former 1630 'gain' (the duchy was occupied, not yet Swedish); mirrors duchy-of-pomerania L8.

region.text: German and western Polish land held by the Swedish armies after Breitenfeld and Rain

ledger.note: April 1632: Swedish armies hold ground in Germany after 'victories at Breitenfeld in September 1631, then Rain in April 1632' (the page: he 'invaded southern Germany'). Cliopatria draws the zone (917 cells) 1632-1635; the real owners of each cell are not on the page. Raised from confidence 1 by the Thirty Years' War page.

1635: Sweden gives up the Prussian ports. 'In 1635, the truce was extended by the Treaty of Stuhmsdorf'; 'Sweden gave up the Prussian ports, and Poland ceded most of Livonia with Riga but kept the Latgale region.'

region.text: the Prussian ports

Raised from confidence 1 by the Thirty Years' War page; was dated 1636.

region.text: The same German zone
the Duchy of Pomerania

ledger.note: 10 March 1637: 'Death of Duke Bogislaw XIV: 10 March 1637' (infobox); 'the last Griffin duke had died during the Thirty Years' War in 1637'. The occupation of 1630 becomes Swedish rule over the part Sweden keeps. Mirrors duchy-of-pomerania L9.

region.text: Western Pomerania, as Cliopatria's 1648 shape holds it

ledger.note: 10 March 1637: the duchy ends and 'was partitioned between Brandenburg-Prussia and Sweden'; Western Pomerania is the part Sweden keeps (Westphalia, 24 October 1648: Sweden 'received ... the imperial territories of Swedish Pomerania', Thirty Years' War page). The single gain of Western Pomerania in this ledger: the former October 1648 gain from the already dissolved duchy is removed. Year is the page's, the region my reading. Mirrors duchy-of-pomerania L10.

region.text: Farther Pomerania (Hinterpommern)

ledger.note: March 1637: Swedish troops hold the rest of the duchy against Brandenburg's inheritance claim. Westphalia: 'Brandenburg-Prussia received Farther Pomerania (Hinterpommern)' in 1648, but 'The recess of Stettin in 1653 settled the border with Brandenburg'; brandenburg-prussia L2/L5/L6 record the contest 1648-1653 and its gain in 1653. Cliopatria never draws Farther Pomerania Swedish, so it is an occupation (hatched); the pages do not date the Swedish withdrawal beyond 1653.

April 1639: Banér carries the war into Saxony and Bohemia. 'In April 1639, Banér defeated the Saxons at Chemnitz, then invaded Bohemia in May.' Region is the Cliopatria 1640 zone, the researcher's reading.

region.text: Saxony and the Bohemian frontier held by Banér's army

ledger.note: December 1642: Leipzig falls. 'The Swedes captured Leipzig in December, although they failed to take Freiberg' (the fetch summary placed it in 1642). Region: Cliopatria's 1642 zone beyond that of 1640.

region.text: Leipzig and the German land round it
the prince-archbishopric of Bremen between the Weser and the Elbe

ledger.note: 'in the Danish-Swedish Torstenson War of 1643–1645 the Swedes seized de facto rule in both prince-bishoprics', so 'Frederick II had to resign as Administrator' (he was 'a son of King Christian IV of Denmark and Norway'). The page gives the span 1643-1645, not a month; 1643 follows prince-archbishopric-of-bremen L10. The cession of 13 August 1645 (Brömsebro) only confirms it: 'the two Swedish occupied prince-bishoprics, were ceded into Swedish hands'. Replaces the former 1645 'gain' from denmark-norway, so Bremen is gained once, in 1648.

region.text: the prince-bishopric of Verden

ledger.note: As for Bremen: the Swedes 'seized de facto rule in both prince-bishoprics' in the Torstenson War (1643-1645); the Danish administrator Frederick II resigned. No Verden dossier event mirrors it (prince-bishopric-of-verden records only its secularisation in 1648).
13 August 1645: the Treaty of Brömsebro gives Sweden Gotland and Ösel. 'Denmark-Norway ceded' Gotland and the island of Saaremaa (Ösel); it ended the Torstenson War.

region.text: the Baltic islands of Gotland and Saaremaa (Ösel)

ledger.note: 13 August 1645: Jämtland and Härjedalen pass from Norway to Sweden. 'Denmark-Norway ceded the Norwegian provinces of' Jämtland and Härjedalen; Idre and Särna, taken by Dalecarlian peasants, were not formally recognised until 1751.

region.text: the Norwegian provinces of Jämtland and Härjedalen

ledger.note: 13 August 1645: Sweden holds Halland for 30 years. 'Sweden received the Danish province of Halland for a period of 30 years as a guarantee of these provisions.'

region.text: the Danish province of Halland, held as a guarantee

ledger.note: 24 October 1648: the Peace of Westphalia ends the Swedish hold on Saxony and Bohemia; page silent on the evacuation, Cliopatria drops the zone in 1648. 'on 24 October he signed peace treaties with France and Sweden, ending the war.'

region.text: Saxony and the Bohemian frontier

ledger.note: 24 October 1648: the Peace of Westphalia ends the Swedish hold on Leipzig and the German zone of the 1640s; page silent on the evacuation.

region.text: Leipzig and the German land round it

ledger.note: 24 October 1648: Sweden gets Wismar. Infobox 'Sweden gains Wismar, Wolin, Western Pomerania, and Bremen-Verden'.

region.text: Wismar
the prince-archbishopric of Bremen

ledger.note: 24 October 1648: the Peace of Westphalia turns the occupied archbishopric into Swedish territory ('transformed by the Peace of Westphalia in 1648 into the Duchy of Bremen'); the Bremen page's infobox dates the secularisation to 15 May 1648, which prince-archbishopric-of-bremen L11/L12 use, so the neighbour's month differs from this ledger's.
24 October 1648: Sweden gets the Duchy of Bremen. 'the Prince-bishoprics of Bremen and Verden, which also gave them a seat in the Imperial Diet'.

region.text: the Duchy of Bremen between the Weser and the Elbe
the prince-bishopric of Verden

24 October 1648: Sweden gets the Principality of Verden (see the Bremen entry for the page's wording).

region.text: the Principality of Verden
Farther Pomerania (Hinterpommern)

ledger.note: 1653: 'The recess of Stettin in 1653 settled the border with Brandenburg in a manner favourable to Sweden'; Farther Pomerania passes to Brandenburg-Prussia (brandenburg-prussia L6 dates the gain to 1653; swedish-pomerania L7 to 4 May 1653). The Swedish Empire page also calls 1653 'the Treaty of Stettin', against 'the Treaty of Stettin (1630)'. No separate loss: the land was only held.

region.text: Greater Poland, Masovia with Warsaw, Lesser Poland with Kraków and Royal Prussia with Thorn, Elbing and Marienburg

ledger.note: 21 July 1655: Wittenberg's division 'entered Poland'; 'the nobles surrendered to Wittenberg on 25 July in Ujście' (Greater Poland), 'On 8 September Charles X Gustav occupied Warsaw', 'Kraków surrendered ... on 19 October', and Thorn, Elbing and 'Marienburg (Malbork) surrendered in March' 1656. By 1658 the Swedish-held ground 'had been reduced to some towns in Royal Prussia'. Region is my reading; Cliopatria does not draw it. The Commonwealth dossier (eu-15) must mirror it.

region.text: the Baltic edge Cliopatria's 1659 shape lacks (Cliopatria 1653 shape minus its 1659 shape, minus the Gold Coast): Nöteborg and Nyenschantz in Ingria, Dorpat, Koknese and Aluksne in Livonia, Nyslott in Finland

ledger.note: July 1656: 'a reserve force of the Russian army struck across Swedish Ingria and overran two key Baltic fortresses' (Nöteborg and Nyenschantz); Dorpat 'fell in October'; Daugavpils and Koknese were taken. The Valiesar truce of 20 December 1658 left Russia 'Koknese, Aluksne, Dorpat, Nyslott' for three years, and Swedes 'recaptured much of Ingria' in 1657, so the Ingrian cells of the region are probably too wide. Region: the land Cliopatria's 1659 shape drops; no tsardom-of-russia event mirrors it.

region.text: the Duchy of Courland and Semigallia

ledger.note: 1658: 'The Swedish army captured Duke Jacob (1658–1660)' (Courland page; 'In 1655, the Swedish army entered the territory of the Duchy'). Extent not described. Mirrors duchy-of-courland L1.
8 March 1658: the Treaty of Roskilde turns the Halland pledge into a cession. 'Halland was on lease to Sweden for a term of 30 years.'

region.text: the Danish province of Halland

ledger.note: 8 March 1658: Denmark-Norway cedes Scania, Blekinge, Halland and Bornholm. The treaty was 'concluded on 26 February (OS) or 8 March 1658 (NS)': 'The immediate cession of the Danish province Scania to Sweden', the same for Blekinge, Halland and Bornholm. Cliopatria shows it from 1659.

region.text: the Danish provinces Scania, Blekinge, Halland and Bornholm

ledger.note: 8 March 1658: Denmark-Norway cedes Bohuslän and Trøndelag. 'The immediate cession of the Norwegian province of Bohuslän to Sweden'; Trøndelag 'then including Nordmøre and Romsdal'; Denmark-Norway 'was forced to give up a third of its territory to save the rest'.

region.text: the Norwegian provinces of Bohuslän and Trøndelag with Nordmøre and Romsdal
the Polish and Royal Prussian ground still held

ledger.note: 23 April 1660, the Treaty of Oliva: 'All occupied territories were restored to their pre-war sovereigns' and 'Sweden was accepted as sovereign in Swedish Livonia'; 'John II Casimir withdrew his claims to the Swedish throne'. The Courland page: 'This war ended with the peace Treaty of Oliwa (1660).'

region.text: the Duchy of Courland and Semigallia

ledger.note: 23 April 1660: Oliva restores 'all occupied territories', which for Courland ends the capture of Duke Jacob (Courland page '1658–1660'). Mirrors duchy-of-courland L2.

27 May 1660: the Treaty of Copenhagen returns Trøndelag and Bornholm. 'Sweden had to relinquish the Norwegian province of Trøndelag and the Danish island of Bornholm'; Sweden kept the Scanian provinces and Bohuslän. The Roskilde page: restored 'in 1660'.

region.text: the Norwegian province of Trøndelag and the Danish island of Bornholm

the Baltic edge Cliopatria's 1659 shape lacks (Cliopatria 1653 shape minus its 1659 shape, minus the Gold Coast): Nöteborg and Nyenschantz in Ingria, Dorpat, Koknese and Aluksne in Livonia, Nyslott in Finland

ledger.note: 2 July 1661, the Treaty of Cardis (Swedish Empire page): the Tsar 'surrendered the Baltic provinces to Sweden'; the war page: Russia was obliged to 'yield its occupied Livonian and Ingrian territories', confirming Stolbovo. This is not a gain: Sweden held Estonia, Ingria and Kexholm from 1617 and Livonia from 1622, and only the land Russia occupied in 1656-1658 comes back (the former region 'Ingria, Estonia and Kexholm' was too wide).

1675: the Scanian War takes Swedish Germany. 'In 1675, Swedish Pomerania and the Duchy of Bremen were taken by the Brandenburgers, Austrians, and Danes'; Stettin fell in December 1677, Stralsund on 15 October 1678, Greifswald on 5 November 1678. Cliopatria does not draw it.

region.text: Swedish Pomerania and the Duchy of Bremen

ledger.note: 29 June 1679: Swedish Germany is restored. Treaties of Nijmegen (7 February) and St. Germain: 'Sweden received almost full restitution of its German territory'; Denmark-Norway returned what it had captured on 4 October 1679 (Fontainebleau and Lund).

region.text: Swedish Pomerania and the Duchy of Bremen
the strip of Farther Pomerania east of the Oder with Gollnow

ledger.note: 29 June 1679, Saint-Germain: 'Sweden received almost full restitution of its German territory', but Brandenburg kept Gollnow and the strip on the east bank of the Oder (the Swedish Pomerania page: held 'as a pawn' until paid in 1693; brandenburg-prussia L9 records it as a gain). Region: Cliopatria's 1670 shape minus its 1683 shape, 8 cells; the page disagreement is in the notes.

1703: Ingria falls to Russia. 'Russian victories at Erastfer and Nöteborg (Shlisselburg) provided access to Ingria in 1703' and Peter 'captured the Swedish fortress of Nyen, guarding the mouth of the River Neva'. The region is Cliopatria's loss between its 1702 and 1706 shapes minus the Narva circle; the rest of its 66 cells is undated on the pages opened. Tartu and Narva have their own events below.

region.text: Ingria and the eastern edge of Estonia and Livonia, without Narva
Tartu (Dorpat)

ledger.note: 24 June 1704: 'Marshal Boris Sheremetev's force of 20,000 captured Tartu on 24 June.' Cliopatria keeps Tartu Swedish until 1713; the keyframes from 1704 take it out. Not mirrored in tsardom-of-russia.

region.text: Narva and Ivangorod

ledger.note: 20 August 1704: 'the Russians captured Narva on 20 August 1704'; the city was 'incorporated into the Russian Tsardom' after an oath of 11 September. Inside Cliopatria's 1703-1706 drop (14 cells). Not mirrored in tsardom-of-russia.
1706: Charles XII invades Saxony. 'he finally had to invade Augustus' hereditary Saxony to take him out of the war'; the Treaty of Altranstädt is dated October 1706.

region.text: Saxony

ledger.note: 1707: Charles XII leaves Saxony. 'Charles XII moved from Saxony into Russia to confront Peter' (1707); Cliopatria draws the strip to 1708.

region.text: Saxony

ledger.note: 1710: Riga and Livonia fall to Russia. 'In 1710 the Russian forces captured Riga.'

region.text: Livonia with Riga

ledger.note: Autumn 1710: Estonia falls to Russia. 'the last city, Tallinn, falling in the autumn of 1710.'

region.text: Estonia with Tallinn (Reval)

ledger.note: 1710: Vyborg falls to Russia. 'Russia captured Viborg in 1710.'

region.text: Viborg
Swedish Bremen-Verden

ledger.note: 1712: 'In 1712, during the Great Northern War ... Denmark-Norway occupied plague stricken Bremen-Verden.' Replaces the former 1713 'loss to Denmark-Norway of Swedish Germany' (confidence 1), which also gave the southern Pomeranian land to Denmark; Cliopatria drops Bremen-Verden in 1713. Mirrors denmark-norway L28 and bremen-verden L5.
1714: Russia occupies Finland, the Great Wrath. 'By 1714, Russia had occupied Finland'; 'The brutal occupation period of Finland in 1714-1721 is known as the Great Wrath'; Napue in February 1714.

region.text: Finland
Swedish Bremen-Verden

ledger.note: 1715: Denmark-Norway ends its occupation by selling the duchies to George I: 'In return for George I's aid, Denmark-Norway sold to him Bremen-Verden, which it kept under occupation since 1712'; the Electorate of Hanover page: 'In 1715, he purchased the duchies of Bremen-Verden from King Frederick IV of Denmark'. Mirrors denmark-norway L30.

region.text: Swedish Bremen-Verden

ledger.note: 1715: Hanover takes de facto possession by the purchase (infobox 'Acquired Bremen-Verden: 1715'); Sweden has not ceded it, which happens in 1719. Mirrors electorate-of-hanover L3.

region.text: southern Swedish Pomerania: Swedish land south of the Peene round Wolgast, Anklam and Usedom (Cliopatria 1709 shape minus its 1721 shape)

ledger.note: 1715: 'Brandenburg-Prussia openly joined the coalition by declaring war on Sweden in the summer of 1715' (Great Northern War page); the Swedish Pomerania page: 'The Danes seized Rügen and Western Pomerania north of the Peene River', the areas south of it 'were taken by Prussia'. Month not on the pages. Replaces the former 1713 'loss to Denmark-Norway'; Cliopatria drops the land in 1713, two years early. Mirrors kingdom-of-prussia L4.

region.text: northern Swedish Pomerania: Stralsund and Rügen, north of the Peene

ledger.note: Rügen fell in November 1715 ('a combined Danish-Saxon-Prussian army landed at Groß Stresow and took the island of Rügen') and Stralsund on 24 December: 'From 12 July to 24 December 1715, the allies sieged the town and eventually forced its surrender'. A Dano-Prussian treaty 'partitioned Swedish Pomerania along the Peene', Denmark getting the north: 'Stralsund became the capital of Danish Pomerania'. Cliopatria keeps it Swedish. Not mirrored in denmark-norway (eu-14-g).

region.text: Wismar

ledger.note: 1716: 'Also in 1716, Swedish Wismar surrendered to the allies, eliminating Sweden's last stronghold on the southern Baltic coast' (the Great Northern War page: 'When Wismar surrendered in 1716, all of Sweden's Baltic and German possessions were lost'). Neither page names the captor: denmark-norway is a guess among the allies, hence confidence 1. Cliopatria keeps Wismar Swedish.

region.text: Swedish Bremen-Verden

ledger.note: 1719: Sweden cedes Bremen-Verden: 'Hanover gained Swedish Bremen-Verden' in the treaties of 1719 (Great Northern War page); the Bremen-Verden page: 'the Treaty of Stockholm of 1719'. Mirrors electorate-of-hanover L4.
1719: Bremen-Verden goes to Hanover. 'Hanover gained Swedish Bremen-Verden' under the Swedish-Hanoverian Treaty of Stockholm (1719).

region.text: Swedish Bremen-Verden
southern Swedish Pomerania

ledger.note: 21 January 1720: the Treaty of Stockholm; 'Prussia had been allowed to retain its conquest, including Stettin' (Swedish Pomerania page). Mirrors kingdom-of-prussia L5.

region.text: southern Swedish Pomerania with Stettin

ledger.note: 21 January 1720: the Treaty of Stockholm with Prussia ('Prussia had been allowed to retain its conquest, including Stettin' on the Swedish Pomerania page; 'Brandenburg-Prussia incorporated southern Swedish Pomerania' on the Great Northern War page, which dates the treaties to 1719 and early 1720). The region is now the 14 cells of southern Swedish Pomerania, not the whole of Pomerania. Mirrors kingdom-of-prussia L6.

region.text: Wismar

ledger.note: 1721: Wismar returns to Sweden; no opened page dates it (the Wismar page is silent on 1715-1721). The year is Cliopatria's 1721 shape, which holds Wismar again; a gap, not a fault.

region.text: northern Swedish Pomerania: Stralsund and Rügen

ledger.note: 17 January 1721: 'Denmark returned its Pomeranian territories to Swedish administration on 17 January 1721' (Swedish Pomerania page); the Stralsund page: 'Stralsund remained under Danish control until it was returned to Sweden by the Treaty of Frederiksborg' (June 1720 on the Great Northern War page). Mirrors swedish-pomerania L14.
10 September 1721 (30 August O.S.): Finland is given back. At the Treaty of Nystad 'Finland was returned to Sweden'.

region.text: Finland

ledger.note: 10 September 1721: the Treaty of Nystad confirms the loss of the Baltic provinces. Sweden ceded 'Estonia, Livonia, Ingria, Kexholm and a portion of Karelia'; the land had been Russian de facto since 1703-1710.

region.text: Estonia, Livonia, Ingria, Kexholm and part of Karelia

ledger.note: 18 August 1743: the Treaty of Åbo moves the border to the Kymi River. Sweden 'ceded to Russia the areas east of the Kymi River with the fortress of Olofsborg' and 'the towns of Villmanstrand (Lappeenranta) and Fredrikshamn (Hamina)'.

region.text: the areas east of the Kymi River with Olofsborg, Villmanstrand and Fredrikshamn
Prussian Pomerania on the Peene: Anklam, Usedom, Wollin, Demmin

ledger.note: 13 September 1757: Sweden 'invaded Prussian Pomerania' (declaration of war 22 September 1757); the Swedes took Peenemünde, reached Anklam and held Usedom and Wollin until they 'withdrew into Swedish Pomerania' in late 1759, and the war lasted to 1762. Not mirrored in kingdom-of-prussia; Cliopatria draws none of it except the 12 cells of 1762.

region.text: Prussian Pomerania on the Peene

ledger.note: 22 May 1762: 'The war was formally ended on 22 May 1762 by the Peace of Hamburg between Prussia, Mecklenburg and Sweden'; 'Prussia and Sweden were restored to the status quo ante bellum', and the infobox lists no territorial change.

region.text: the town and lordship of Wismar with Poel and Neukloster

ledger.note: 1803: 'In 1803, Sweden ceded both the town and lordship to the Grand Duchy of Mecklenburg-Schwerin for 1,258,000 Riksdalers' but 'reserved the right of redemption after 100 years'; Sweden renounced its claim in 1903. The page does not name the Treaty of Malmö. Mirrors mecklenburg L8.

region.text: Swedish Pomerania

ledger.note: 1807: the French occupation of Swedish Pomerania 'beginning in 1807' follows Sweden's entry into the Third Coalition in 1805 (month not on the page). Cliopatria keeps it Swedish.

region.text: Finland, occupied by Russia from February 1808

ledger.note: 21 February 1808: 'On February 21, 1808, 24,000 Russian troops ... crossed the Swedish–Russian border'; Helsinki fell on 2 March, Sveaborg on 6 May, and 'By November 1808, Russian forces had overrun all of Finland'. Cliopatria keeps Finland Swedish until 1809.

region.text: Finland

ledger.note: 17 September 1809: the Treaty of Fredrikshamn turns the occupation into a cession (next event).

region.text: Finland

ledger.note: 17 September 1809: 'in which Sweden ceded the whole of Finland and all of its domains east of the Torne river' (Treaty of Fredrikshamn on the Finnish War page; infobox 'Sweden loses Finland, Åland, a part of Lapland and a part of West Bothnia'). The Swedish Empire page says only 'ceded to Russia in 1809'. Cliopatria's 1809 shape holds 5 Finnish cells of the Torne valley.

region.text: Swedish Pomerania

ledger.note: 1810: 'Under the Treaty of Paris, signed in 1810, the territory was returned to Sweden' (Swedish Pomerania page; month not given).

4 November 1814: the Swedish Empire row ends as Sweden and Norway unite. The Treaty of Kiel (14 January 1814) gave Norway to the Swedish king for Swedish Pomerania; Norway declared independence, a brief war ended in a ceasefire, Norway accepted a personal union by the Convention of Moss (August 1814), and 'The Storting elected Charles XIII as king of Norway on 4 November 1814, formally establishing the union'. Swedish Pomerania stayed Swedish until 23 October 1815.

region.text: Sweden, with Swedish Pomerania until 1815

wars.name: Ingrian War
wars.outcome: Treaty of Stolbovo, 9 March 1617: Sweden gains Kexholm and Ingria, Novgorod and other gains are returned, Russia renounces Estonia and Livonia.
wars.note: 'a peace treaty that ended the Ingrian War, which had been fought between the Swedish Empire and the Russian Tsardom between 1610 and 1617.'

wars.name: Kalmar War
wars.outcome: Treaty of Knäred, 20 January 1613: all conquests returned, Sweden pays 1 million rixdollars as ransom for Älvsborg, which Denmark-Norway holds meanwhile.
wars.note: 'The Kalmar War (1611–1613) was fought between' Denmark–Norway and Sweden; 'in April 1611 ... Denmark–Norway declared war upon Sweden and invaded'.

wars.name: Polish-Swedish War (1621-1625)

zones.text: Livonia north of the Daugava with Riga

wars.outcome: Truce of Mitawa, November 1622: the Commonwealth cedes Livonia north of the Daugava; the war resumes in 1625 and Sweden 'now controlled the line of the Daugava'.
wars.note: Infobox: 'Swedish victory'; 'Territorial changes: Commonwealth cedes Livonia north of the Daugava river'.

wars.name: Polish-Swedish War (1626-1629)

zones.text: Livonia north of the Daugava with Riga

wars.outcome: Truce of Altmark, 26 September 1629: Sweden keeps Livonia down to the Daugava including Riga and the Prussian coastal cities, which it returns in 1635 (Stuhmsdorf).
wars.note: 'ending the Polish-Swedish War (1626-1629)'; Swedish conquests of 1621-1625 are not described on the page.

wars.name: Thirty Years' War

zones.text: the German zone held by Swedish armies 1632-1635

wars.outcome: Peace of Westphalia, 24 October 1648: Sweden gains Western Pomerania, Wolin, Wismar, Bremen-Verden and five million thalers; the armies' other conquests are given up.
wars.note: Sweden's part runs from the landing in Pomerania in June 1630; the war as a whole is 23 May 1618 to 24 October 1648. The Swedish-Polish front is the Truce of Altmark's, extended at Stuhmsdorf in 1635.

wars.name: Torstenson War
wars.outcome: Treaty of Brömsebro, 13 August 1645: Jämtland, Härjedalen, Gotland and Ösel to Sweden, Halland for 30 years, Bremen and Verden under Swedish control.
wars.note: 'ended the Torstenson War, a local conflict that began in 1643 (and was part of the larger Thirty Years' War)'.

wars.name: Second Northern War (Polish front)

zones.text: Greater Poland, Warsaw, Kraków and Royal Prussia

wars.outcome: Treaty of Oliva, 23 April 1660: 'All occupied territories were restored to their pre-war sovereigns'; Sweden keeps Livonia.
wars.note: Sweden invaded on 21 July 1655; Warsaw fell on 8 September and Kraków on 19 October 1655. Polish zones wait for the eu-15 dossiers.

wars.name: Russo-Swedish War (1656-1658)

zones.text: the Baltic edge Cliopatria's 1659 shape lacks (Cliopatria 1653 shape minus its 1659 shape, minus the Gold Coast): Nöteborg and Nyenschantz in Ingria, Dorpat, Koknese and Aluksne in Livonia, Nyslott in Finland

wars.outcome: Truce of Valiesar, 20 December 1658 (Russia keeps Koknese, Aluksne, Dorpat and Nyslott for three years); Treaty of Cardis, 2 July 1661: Russia yields the occupied Livonian and Ingrian territories.
wars.note: Infobox 'July 1656–1658/1661'; 'Already in May 1656, Alexis of Russia had declared war on Sweden.'

wars.name: Second Northern War (Danish front)
wars.outcome: Treaty of Roskilde, 8 March 1658: Scania, Blekinge, Halland, Bohuslän, Trøndelag and Bornholm to Sweden; second Swedish attack, Copenhagen attacked, Charles forced to withdraw in 1659; Treaty of Copenhagen, 27 May 1660: Bornholm and Trøndelag returned.
wars.note: The page gives no start year for the war; the invasion of Zealand began on 11 February 1658. The Russian front (1656-1661) is not on the pages opened.

wars.name: Scanian War

zones.text: Swedish Pomerania and the Duchy of Bremen

wars.outcome: Nijmegen (7 February 1679), St. Germain (29 June 1679), Fontainebleau (2 September) and Lund (4 October): almost full restitution of Sweden's German territory.
wars.note: Stettin fell in December 1677, Stralsund on 15 October 1678, Greifswald on 5 November 1678.

wars.name: Great Northern War
wars.outcome: Treaty of Nystad, 10 September 1721: Sweden loses Estonia, Livonia, Ingria, Kexholm and part of Karelia, keeps Finland; Stockholm 1719-1720: Hanover gets Bremen-Verden, Prussia southern Swedish Pomerania.
wars.note: 22 February 1700 to 10 September 1721 (infobox). Pages disagree on the Danish hold of northern Swedish Pomerania ('Danish from 1712 to 1715' against Stralsund falling in December 1715 and Wismar surrendering in 1716).

wars.name: Russo-Swedish War (1741-1743)

zones.text: the areas east of the Kymi River

wars.outcome: Treaty of Åbo, 18 August 1743: Sweden cedes the land east of the Kymi River, Villmanstrand and Fredrikshamn; Russia had occupied most of Finland.
wars.note: 'in the end of the Russo-Swedish War of 1741-1743'.

wars.name: Pomeranian War

zones.text: Prussian Pomerania on the Peene: Anklam, Usedom, Wollin, Demmin

wars.outcome: Peace of Hamburg, 22 May 1762: Prussia and Sweden 'restored to the status quo ante bellum'.
wars.note: 'On September 13 that force invaded Prussian Pomerania.'

wars.name: Russo-Swedish War (1788-1790)

zones.text: the Finnish-Russian frontier (the page read gives no places; no land changed hands)

wars.outcome: Treaty of Värälä, 14 August 1790: status quo ante bellum, 'All conquests made by both sides are returned'.

wars.name: Finnish War
wars.outcome: Treaty of Fredrikshamn, 17 September 1809: Sweden cedes Finland, Åland, a part of Lapland and a part of West Bothnia.
wars.note: 'On February 21, 1808, 24,000 Russian troops ... crossed the Swedish–Russian border'.

wars.name: Swedish-Norwegian war of 1814
wars.outcome: A brief war ended in a ceasefire and the Convention of Moss (August 1814); Norway accepted a personal union, formed on 4 November 1814.
wars.note: The page gives no dates for the war or the convention beyond August 1814 and the union on 4 November; Norway was never Swedish territory.

certainty.note: Conquests, truces and army-held German zones; the Lapland and Norwegian frontiers are unsurveyed throughout the empire's life.
Treaty lines: Copenhagen 1660, Oliva 1660, Cardis 1661, St. Germain and Lund 1679; the Scanian and Great Northern War occupations are the exceptions and soft.
The Great Wrath: Finland occupied, Swedish Germany partitioned, the front moving.
Nystad 1721, the Kymi River border of Åbo 1743, Fredrikshamn 1809, Kiel 1814; only the Lapland frontier stays soft.

notes:
Swedish Empire as an era of the Kingdom of Sweden. The kingdom-of-sweden dossier (this group, another part) decided on no break: one state from about 980, with Cliopatria's Kalmar Union, Swedish Empire and United Kingdoms rows drawn over the same crown. This dossier reviews the 25 shapes of the Cliopatria row 'Swedish Empire' (1612-1814) and keeps the Cliopatria years: the Swedish Empire page itself ends the empire in 1721 ('its end as the loss of territories in 1721'), but the row runs to the union with Norway in 1814. Proposal for the colour agent: give this dossier the same family (nordic) and the same colour as kingdom-of-sweden; Sweden's colour must not change in 1612 or in 1814. It could also be merged into that dossier.
OVERLAPS: the Swedish possessions have their own colony dossiers (swedish-estonia, swedish-ingria, swedish-livonia, kexholm-county, swedish-pomerania, bremen-verden, swedish-gold-coast, new-sweden). Cliopatria's Swedish Empire shape already contains the first six, so the compiler must not draw them twice. The Gold Coast cells (1653-1658, 1662-1669) are removed from the base shape here (keyframe adjust) because the colony dossier carries the years; New Sweden and Saint Barthelemy (Swedish 1784-1878) are in no Cliopatria shape.
OCCUPATION, NOT TERRITORY: Cliopatria draws the land held by Swedish armies in Germany (1632-1635, 1639-1648) and Saxony (1706-1708) as Swedish; the shapes are corrected to the base realm and the zones are ledger occupation events (hatched). The counterparts are the umbrella dossier holy-roman-empire-minor-states and electorate-of-saxony; the real owners of each cell (Bavaria, Brandenburg, Habsburg lands) are not named on the pages opened.
Lags and leads in Cliopatria's years that the pages date: Stolbovo 1617 (shape 1619); Livonia north of the Daugava 1622 (shape 1629); Roskilde 1658 (shape 1659); Copenhagen 1660 (the shape keeps Trøndelag and Bornholm to 1661); Cardis 1661; Tartu and Narva 1704; Livonia and Estonia lost 1710 (shape 1713); Finland occupied 1714 (shape 1718) and again February 1808 (shape 1809); Åbo 1743 (shape 1744); Saxony left 1707 (shape 1709); Bremen-Verden occupied 1712 and southern Pomerania 1715 (the 1713 shape drops both); Stralsund, Rügen and Wismar occupied 1715-1716 but kept in the shapes to 1720. Still unexplained by any opened page: the other 52 of the 66 eastern cells Cliopatria drops in 1706 (only Narva is dated), the 1814 shape's other cells, Saint Barthelemy (Swedish 1784-1878, in no shape).
Page disagreements: the Swedish Empire page dates Swedish Pomerania to 'the Treaty of Stettin (1630)' and elsewhere to 'the Treaty of Stettin in 1653', and says Westphalia granted 'a strip of Farther Pomerania on the right side of the Oder' while the Swedish Pomerania page has Sweden restored in 1679 except Gollnow and the east-bank strip, held by Brandenburg 'as a pawn' until paid in 1693 (brandenburg-prussia records it as a 1679 gain; the ledger loss is confidence 2). The Altmark page says 26 September 1629 (O.S. 16 September) and its reference title 12 September. The Great Northern War page has Stralsund fall in December 1715 and Wismar in 1716 yet says the Stockholm treaties 'assured that Sweden was to retain Wismar and northern Swedish Pomerania', dates the Prussian treaty both 1719 and early 1720, and puts Frederiksborg in June 1720, while the Swedish Pomerania page has Denmark return its Pomeranian territories on 17 January 1721. The Swedish Empire page gives Treaty of Cardis 'Ingria, Estonia and Kexholm' although Sweden held Estonia from 1617; the ledger returns only the land Russia occupied. Nystad is 30 August O.S., 10 September N.S.
Area check: the Swedish Empire page has no infobox area; its body text says 'The land area of Sweden was 1,100,000 km2.' with no year (read as the realm after Cardis, 1661), against 921,329 km2 for the 1662 shape: ratio 0.84.
Page budget: the 9 pages of the first pass were exceeded in the repair pass of 2026-11-01, which opened the 18 further pages now in sources[] to apply the reviewer's findings (the reviewer did not fail the dossier for budget). 1762 is now checked against the Pomeranian War page and 1763-1806 against the Russo-Swedish War of 1788-1790 page; the Gold Coast is still 'unverified'. Regions the gazetteer lacks: Wismar, Gdov and Anklam (places), Bohuslän, Härjedalen, Kexholm, Verden or Bremen-Verden (regions), Bornholm (island); coordinates and radii were used for some of them.
Norway in 1814 is a personal union; no ledger gain was written for it (rule 4: associations are never territory); the kingdom-of-norway and united-kingdoms-of-sweden-and-norway dossiers carry it.
REPAIR PASS 2026-11-01: Pomerania is occupied in 1630 and gained once, as Western Pomerania, in March 1637, with Farther Pomerania held as an occupation against Brandenburg from 1637 to 1653; Bremen-Verden is occupied from 1643 and gained once, in October 1648; the 1713 'loss to Denmark-Norway' is replaced by the Danish (1712-1715), Hanoverian (1715-1719) and Prussian (1715-1720) occupations and the Danish occupation of northern Swedish Pomerania (December 1715-January 1721) and Wismar (1716-1721); the Russian occupation of the Baltic edge 1656-1661 replaces the Cardis 'gain'; the Kalmar War, Novgorod and Gdov, Livonia 1621-1622, the Polish front of the Second Northern War, Courland 1658-1660, Tartu and Narva 1704, the strip east of the Oder 1679, Wismar 1803, the French occupation 1807-1810, the Finnish War, the Pomeranian War and the Russo-Swedish wars of 1656 and 1788 are added; Guadeloupe leaves the 1814 shape; rulers run to 1814. Mirrors that the neighbours still lack: denmark-norway (northern Swedish Pomerania and Wismar 1715-1721), tsardom-of-russia (1656-1661, Tartu and Narva 1704), polish-lithuanian-commonwealth (Livonia 1621-1622, the Polish front 1655-1660), kingdom-of-prussia (Pomeranian War 1757-1762) and first-french-empire (Swedish Pomerania 1807-1810).
